subject: Pilot scope & role commitments: Northshore private deployment strawman
messages:
From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai

Cc: julia.park@northshore.com, procurement@northshore.com
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot scope & role commitments: Northshore private deployment strawman

Team —

Thanks for aligning earlier this week. Per our sync with Northshore (Julia), I pulled together a concise strawman for a 6-week private (VPC + on-prem connector) pilot. Attached is a runbook draft and a short prep checklist. High-level ask: can each of you confirm the resourcing commitments below by EOD Tuesday so we can finalize the SOW and procurement timeline?

Strawman summary (6 weeks):
- Week 0: Legal & procurement complete, customer network approvals and firewall rules in place
- Week 1: Infra prep (VPC peering, VPN, initial infra IaC), deploy control plane in isolated subnet
- Week 2: Model onboarding (quantization profile + runtime tests) + security review evidence handoff
- Week 3: Integration test (prefix caching, KV cache behavior under sample load)
- Week 4: Performance tuning & stress run (SLA smoke tests)
- Week 5: Cutover rehearsal + customer validation
- Week 6: Pilot close, handoff to customer success + runbook finalization

Role/ask checklist (what I need you to commit):
- Karthik: technical lead for infra & runtime tuning; ~0.4 FTE for the pilot window, ad-hoc for pre-run tests
- Grace: ops lead for runbook, on-call rota, and perf smoke tests; ~0.3 FTE plus one on-call engineer during stress run
- Monica: customer success/PM lead to drive acceptance criteria, coordinate customer participants, and own cutover plan; ~0.2 FTE

Key open items for decision:
1) Do we accept Northshore's request for persistent audit logs retained for 12 months in their on-prem storage? (security/legal)
2) Do we run the pilot on a dedicated small GPU pool or allow burst into shared pool for the stress run (cost vs predictability)?
3) Who owns the post-pilot remediation bucket for things that require engineering tasks beyond pilot scope?

Attachments: northshore_pilot_runbook_v1.pdf (draft), prep_checklist.xlsx

Julia — feel free to add any must-have acceptance criteria. Team — please reply with your commitments and any blockers. If we can lock this by Tuesday EOD, procurement can aim for a Week 0 start the following week.

-Chloe
Chloe Martin

Subject: Re: Pilot scope & role commitments: Northshore private deployment strawman

Chloe — thanks for the clear strawman and the artifacts. Quick tech notes + resource ask after a skim:

Technical clarifications / assumptions:
- Persistent audit logs to customer storage: feasible, but we need an ops runbook step and a short-lived agent to ship logs securely (SFTP / HTTPS push). That adds ~1 week of infra work if we need encryption/hsm integration.
- Model onboarding: to validate quantization profiles we need a representative 100k-token corpus from Northshore and 2 full inference passes under load; ask customer to provide by Week 1 cutover.
- Dedicated pool vs shared burst: for pilot predictability I'd recommend a small dedicated pool (1 GPU node equivalent) for the stress run week; shared-burst risks noisy neighbors and non-deterministic perf. Cost delta is modest given pilot duration.

My resource estimate (rough):
- Pre-run infra + network validation: 2 engineers x 3 days (IaC and firewall rules)
- Model quantization & validation: 1 engineer x 5 days + 0.5 infra for perf tests
- Runtime tuning & stress harness: 1 engineer x 4 days + ops on-call during the run

Blockers I see: customer needs to confirm token corpus and allow us access to a staging blob endpoint for model artifacts; also need SOC evidence for the log-shipping approach if they require 12-month retention.

I can own technical lead as requested — I confirm ~0.4 FTE across the pilot window, but will need one additional engineer (preferably someone familiar with our quantized-runtime flow) as a backup for the stress run.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Short note from ops perspective:

Agree with Karthik on dedicated pool for the stress run. A couple of operational constraints to flag so the SOW is realistic:
- On-call coverage: our standard on-call rotation requires a minimum 24-hour handover window between shifts; for the stress run week we should schedule two named engineers instead of relying on ad-hoc coverage.
- Runbook completeness: the attached runbook looks good but needs clear escalation matrix entries (pager contacts and escalation times) and a rollback checklist for the cutover rehearsal. I added inline comments in the Drive doc (link above).
- Audit log retention: if Northshore requires 12 months on-prem, we must specify responsibility for storage costs and egress (if we need to retrieve logs). Request legal to confirm whether this becomes a billable item or sits with the customer.

I'll own runbook updates (Grace) and create the on-call rota draft. Commitment: ~0.35 FTE for pilot coordination, plus two named on-call engineers for stress run week (names TBC).

-grace

Confirmed decisions:
- Pilot window: 6 weeks starting Week 0 once procurement signs off. Target Week 0 start: 2026-11-22 if procurement completes approvals this week.
- Dedicated GPU pool for stress run: approved (Karthik recommendation).
- Audit logs: we will support 12-month retention on customer-managed storage, customer pays storage costs; Legal to confirm contract language.

Owners and immediate actions (owners - due dates):
- Karthik: prepare IaC and firewall template + estimate for additional engineer (due 2026-11-12)
- Grace: finalize runbook with escalation matrix and draft on-call rota (due 2026-11-12)
- Monica: finalize acceptance criteria with Julia and confirm token corpus delivery timeline (due 2026-11-10)
- Chloe: update SOW draft and share final runbook with procurement + Julia (due 2026-11-11)

Meeting: I'll schedule a 30-min sync Wednesday 2026-11-10 10:00-10:30 PT to triage open items — please accept if that works.

Julia — thank you for partnering; Monica will follow up on acceptance criteria and token corpus. If procurement needs anything specific for the SOW (budget line for storage, encryption obligations), tag me and I'll prioritize.
